headline: Dry, mild weather and good holiday travel conditions hold around Mammoth Lakes and across the Sierra through Saturday, then rain and high-elevation snow arrive later Sunday, with a stronger storm and lower snow levels Monday night into Tuesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving stays dry across the eastern Sierra, including the Mammoth Lakes area, and western Nevada, with high pressure overhead and light winds. High and mid-level clouds stream in from the Pacific, and temperatures run warmer than average, with highs in the mid 50s to lower 60s in most areas. Cold air trapped in the valleys each morning may reduce air quality and build haze, and freezing fog is expected around Truckee early this morning and again late tonight. No advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday and Saturday stay dry with highs in the mid 50s to lower 60s in most areas, about 5 to 10 degrees above late-November averages. Friday morning is chilly, with lows mainly in the mid 20s to mid 30s, then thicker clouds keep the next two nights milder. A weak disturbance passing to the north brings west wind gusts up to 60 mph on Sierra ridges Friday into Friday night, and a few light showers near the Oregon border Friday night (only a 20 to 35 percent chance of a tenth of an inch north of Cedarville).

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Rain and high-elevation snow return Sunday, now a bit later, with the best chances later Sunday afternoon through late evening and snow levels around 7,500 to 8,000 feet; this first storm is light, with only a 10 to 25 percent chance of 2 inches or more at main pass levels, but allow extra time on Sierra passes heading home from the holiday weekend, and winds pick up on Sierra ridges Sunday and Sunday night. A potentially more impactful storm arrives by late Monday and continues through Tuesday or Tuesday night, with heavier Sierra snow and snow levels dropping to 5,500 to 6,500 feet, though snow amounts vary widely depending on its track. More storms could follow later next week into the first weekend of December, possibly after a 1 to 3 day break, so plan for periods of winter driving conditions in the Sierra next week.

watch_for: Sierra ridge wind gusts up to 60 mph Friday into Friday night
Snow on Sierra passes later Sunday afternoon and evening during return holiday travel
Track and snow amounts for the stronger Monday night–Tuesday storm
confidence: Confidence is high in dry, mild weather through Saturday; Sunday's light storm is trending later, and snow amounts for the Monday–Tuesday storm and timing of later storms remain uncertain.
